referenceEncoder.name: cbV2G
referenceEncoder.note: Wire-conformant ISO 15118-20 ACDP reference. Each vector is a fixed message emitted by tools/cbv2g-ref/main_iso20.c (run: cbv2g_iso20 ACDP_<name>). Header SessionID is 8x0x00, TimeStamp=1700000000, no Signature. The C# test builds the matching message via Iso15118_20AcdpFixtures and diffs its bytes.

deviatesFromReferenceEncoder.verifiedBy: EXIficient 1.0.4 against ISO's own V2G_CI_ACDP.xsd (decode -> re-encode -> identical octets)
deviatesFromReferenceEncoder.why: ACDP is the only ISO 15118 set with two global elements sharing a named type -- ACDP_DisconnectReq/Res have none of their own and reuse ACDP_ConnectReqType/ResType. cbexigen numbers the document grammar so the type-sharing pair lands adjacent; EXI 1.0 Second Edition 8.5.1 numbers global elements 'sorted lexicographically, first by local-name, then by uri' with no exception for a shared type. The two indices are swapped, which is exactly these two frames: one was unreadable to a schema-following codec and the other decoded cleanly AS THE OTHER MESSAGE. Decided 2026-08-08 to follow the specification; the generator keeps ExiDocumentElementOrder=CbV2GCompatible available and Directory.Build.props records the reasoning. cbV2G's bytes for these two are in git history at 31144ed.
